A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AnyDressing and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures and supplementary material. All 23 pages of each version support comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original benchmark comparisons, ablations, a 40-participant user study and supplementary generation experiments.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results in Tables 1–3 and the main and supplementary figures.

M1.justification: The GFE, DA, IGL and GTL mechanisms and loss/inference equations are retained. However, Figure 2 changes GarmentsNet's frozen-with-LoRA designation to trainable while the GFE text still specifies LoRA-only updates. Whether additional shared weights become trainable is unclear. The newly stated omission of GarmentsNet cross-attention was already depicted in v1.

E1.justification: DressCode/proprietary training data, VITON-HD, Dressing-Pair and supplementary hat, stylized and control scenarios are retained. Although Section 5.1 drops the phrase 'non-garment images,' Figure 3 retains its artwork-conditioned example; inspection does not establish removal of that coverage.

E2.justification: IP-Adapter, StableGarment, MagicClothing and IMAGDressing remain the comparators in Tables 1–2 and the corresponding main and supplementary comparisons. Newly cited DreamFit is not evaluated.

E3.justification: Sample counts, resolution, training budget, optimizer, sampling settings, metrics and user-study procedures match. However, the revised train/frozen annotation and Section 5.1's trainable-module statement do not clearly specify whether shared GarmentsNet weights are optimized differently or existing LoRA training is being relabeled. The extent of this reported training-control revision is therefore uncertain.

E4.justification: Table 3 and Figures 5–6 and 11 retain the same component ablations. Supplementary scalability experiments with hats, garment-combination examples and plugin demonstrations are also retained without additional analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests for the benchmark scores. No seed, repetition-count or uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: All values in Tables 1–3 are identical, including Dressing-Pair scores of 0.296 CLIP-T, 0.734 CLIP-I* and 5.874 CLIP-AS for AnyDressing. Qualitative result images are retained; supplementary figure pages are visually identical.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and derivations remain unchanged. Section 4.1 corrects a mislabeled LoRA symbol in the value projection to the already-defined weight-update symbol; this is a notation correction rather than new mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about multi-garment dressing, the proposed components, plugin compatibility and state-of-the-art performance. Added DreamFit attribution does not alter these main claims.

C2.justification: Section 4.2.1 removes the assertion that frozen attention prevents effective garment–latent relationship capture. Section 4.1 adds a redundancy-based explanation for omitting GarmentsNet cross-attention. Interpretations of the experimental results and supplementary applicability claims otherwise remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 clarifies Stable Diffusion U-Net initialization and discusses trainable modules, but removes the explicit CLIP ViT-L/14 text-encoder specification. Hardware, hyperparameters and the project link remain unchanged. The single-forward-pass statement added to Section 7.1 was already documented in v1 Section 8.

R1.justification: DreamFit is added to the introduction, related work and Section 4.1, where it is credited as inspiration for using LoRA. The CLIP foundational reference is removed with the text-encoder specification. Other reference changes largely reflect renumbering.

P1.justification: There are localized rewrites in the introduction, GarmentsNet description and experimental setup, plus a short supplementary addition. The section sequence and overall narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: Figure 2 revises LoRA placement illustrations, projection blocks, train/frozen markers and the legend. Table 3 moves below Figure 6, with accompanying text reflow. Other result displays and supplementary figure pages are retained.

improvement.justification: DreamFit attribution, more explicit LoRA illustrations and the notation correction improve exposition. However, v2 removes the text-encoder identification and leaves the changed GarmentsNet training designation insufficiently specified. These mixed effects on technical clarity and reproducibility, with unchanged empirical evidence, prevent a reliable judgment of net overall improvement.
